subject: science
passage: Many birds can sleep with one half of the brain at a time, keeping open the eye connected to the waking half. The ability has long been assumed to guard against predators, but testing that idea requires showing that birds use it more when danger is greater. In one experiment, researchers arranged mallard ducks in a row of four and recorded their brain activity and eyes as they slept. Ducks at the two ends of the row, each with an exposed side, spent far more of their sleep with one hemisphere awake than ducks in the middle, and the open eye was almost always the one facing outward, away from the group. When the positions were switched, the behavior switched too. The birds were not simply sleeping lightly; they appeared to be allocating sleep to each half of the brain according to where a threat could come from.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Birds that keep one eye open while sleeping are simply sleeping more lightly than birds with both eyes closed.
choices.B: Mallard ducks prefer to sleep in the middle of a group because that position lets both halves of the brain rest.
choices.C: Ducks at the ends of a row were unable to sleep because of their exposed position.
choices.D: The experiment suggests that ducks adjust which half of the brain sleeps, and how much, according to their exposure to danger.

explanation.why: The text frames the experiment as a test of whether half-brain sleep is "a guard against predators." The results support that idea: end ducks used it more, their open eye faced outward, and the pattern followed the birds when positions changed. The last sentence draws the conclusion that the ducks were "allocating sleep to each half of the brain according to where a threat could come from."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text explicitly rejects this: "The birds were not simply sleeping lightly."
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never discusses which position the ducks prefer; the researchers placed them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The end ducks did sleep; they simply kept one hemisphere awake more often, so this overstates the finding.
explanation.D: Correct. This states the conclusion the experiment supports, with the text's own caution ("appeared").
